description:
The `scripts/validate_submission.py` on the `published-results` branch
(pinned at v0.2.1, commit `0182c9556`) uses a per-DIRECTORY hash
algorithm (`hashlib.sha256()` over `path.encode() + file.read_bytes()`
for every file in `bundle_dir` excluding the manifest). The same
script on `develop` (post-PR #33) uses a per-FILE hash (just
`sha256(bundle_file)` plus a `companion_hashes` map). The writer in
`develop`'s `submit.py` also uses per-file. Result: a bundle produced
by current `develop`'s `benchbox submit` will fail CI on
`published-results` with `Bundle hash mismatch: manifest says XXXX,
computed YYYY`.

This was confirmed empirically during the 2026-04-29 Codex
agent-proxy dry-run:
  - Codex's manifest: `bundle_hash: 799c80a2...` (per-file SHA-256)
  - Validator on published-results computed: `8a89ab6f...` (per-dir)
  - `shasum -a 256` on the actual bundle file: `799c80a2...` (matches
    the manifest exactly)

Forensic and full reproduction at
`_project/handoffs/external-dry-run-retrospective-2026-04-29.md`
(Appendix B).

This is a release-blocker for the community submission flow: until
the validator on `published-results` matches the writer's contract,
no contributor can successfully submit a result regardless of how
closely they follow the docs. The bug is invisible to maintainers
who only run the validator inside `develop`, because both sides
agree there.

anti_patterns.dont: revert develop's writer to per-directory hash
anti_patterns.why: per-file is the right contract for individually-addressable bundles

anti_patterns.instead: the test is the regression-prevention story for this whole class of bug
anti_patterns.why: the same drift will happen again the next time either side changes

preserves.behavior: Backwards-compat with already-merged community submissions in results-data/bundles/ (zero exist today, so this is theoretical)
develop's per-file hash contract (per-file is the right design -- bundles are individually addressable in results-data/bundles/)

scope_rules.path_glob: tests/fixtures/ (only if w3 vendors the validator instead of pulling live)

verifications.command:
git fetch --quiet origin published-results && \
TMP=$(mktemp) && \
git show origin/published-results:scripts/validate_submission.py > "$TMP" && \
python3 "$TMP" /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox/submission/bundle/tpch_sf001_duckdb_sql_20260428_205018_e4f24ee2.json 2>&1 | tail -3; \
rc=$?; rm -f "$TMP"; exit $rc
verifications.description: Validator on published-results passes against a develop-submitted bundle
Cross-branch contract test (added by w3) passes
verifications.expected: All tests pass (test file is created by w3; this verification only meaningful after w3 lands)

work_units.notes:
DECISION: choose path A -- update the `published-results`
validator directly.

Rationale:
  - This is a production submission-flow blocker independent of
    the Python package release cadence: GitHub Actions executes
    `scripts/validate_submission.py` from the PR checkout of the
    `published-results` branch.
  - `develop` already has the correct per-file writer and
    validator contract. Waiting for the release-flow dry run would
    delay contributor submissions without improving the contract.
  - The branch-specific validator fix can be verified immediately
    by running the `published-results` validator against the
    Codex dry-run bundle cited in the retrospective.

`/code review W1`: no required issues. The rejected path B remains
the longer-term release hygiene path, but it is not the fastest
unblock for external contributors.

Two paths:
A. Cherry-pick the post-PR-#33 `scripts/validate_submission.py`
   (and any related changes) onto `published-results`. Quickest
   unblock; doesn't depend on a release.
B. Cut the next benchbox release (per
   `release-flow-dry-run-rc1`) which propagates the validator
   to v0.x.y, then sync `published-results` from the release tag.
Recommend A for speed (the validator is a script, not a wheel
artefact -- it runs from the PR's checkout of published-results
regardless of whether benchbox is installed). B is cleaner long
term but blocks on the release-flow dry-run already in flight.
work_units.summary: Decide path: cherry-pick develop's validator to published-results, or land a release first

work_units.notes:
Applied path A in branch
`fix/published-results-validator-manifest` and opened PR #87
against `published-results`:
https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/87

Scope of the branch-specific patch:
  - `scripts/validate_submission.py` now skips `*.manifest.json`
    during bundle discovery.
  - The validator prefers `<bundle-stem>.manifest.json`, while
    preserving the legacy `submission-manifest.json` fallback.

Verification run against the Codex dry-run bundle cited in the
retrospective:
  - legacy `submission-manifest.json` layout: 0 errors,
    0 warnings.
  - per-bundle `<stem>.manifest.json` layout: 0 errors,
    0 warnings.

`/code review W2`: no required issues. The patch is branch-local,
preserves legacy manifests, and does not touch the writer.

After sync, re-run the validator on `published-results` against
a freshly-submitted bundle:
  cd <published-results checkout>
  python3 scripts/validate_submission.py /path/to/bundle.json
Expected: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
Use the artefacts Codex left at
`/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox/submission/` (or regenerate via
`benchbox submit --last`) for the round-trip.
work_units.summary: Apply chosen path; verify with a round-trip test

work_units.notes:
Already landed before this TODO cleanup:
  - `tests/integration/test_cross_branch_validator_contract.py`
  - `tests/fixtures/published_results_validator.py`

Evidence:
  - `git log -- tests/integration/test_cross_branch_validator_contract.py tests/fixtures/published_results_validator.py`
    shows the contract test and vendored validator landed in
    prior dry-run follow-up commits (#49, #51, #45).
  - `cmp -s scripts/validate_submission.py tests/fixtures/published_results_validator.py`
    returns 0, so the vendored validator matches the develop
    validator byte-for-byte.
  - The test covers writer output, companion hashes, symlink
    rejection, missing-manifest-field UX, and validator drift.

`/code review W3`: no required issues. The original TODO
suggested fetching `origin/published-results` live; the landed
test intentionally vendors the validator to keep the fast lane
deterministic and avoid network/branch-state flake.

Add `tests/integration/test_cross_branch_validator_contract.py`
that validates the writer's emitted hashes match what the
validator on `published-results` computes. Implementation shape:
  - Run `benchbox submit` to produce a bundle + manifest in a
    temp dir.
  - Fetch `scripts/validate_submission.py` from
    `origin/published-results` (via `git show
    origin/published-results:scripts/validate_submission.py`)
    and exec it against the freshly-emitted bundle.
  - Assert no hash mismatch.
Vendor the published-results validator into
`tests/fixtures/` if pulling it live makes the test flaky
(network, branch state). Prevents the same drift from
happening again the next time either side of the contract
changes.
work_units.summary: Add a CI cross-branch contract test to prevent recurrence
